quests.instruction: Maya forgot to water the bean plant on her windowsill for a week. Its leaves are drooping.
quests.question: What does the plant most need?
options: Wind
Snow
Water
Ice
quests.correctAnswer: Water
quests.hint: Soil that has dried out leaves roots with nothing to drink.
quests.explanation: Plants take in water through their roots. Without it, their stems and leaves go limp.
quests.funFact: Plants can lose a lot of water through their leaves on hot days.

quests.instruction: Two identical plants sit in a room. One is by the sunny window and the other is in a dark cupboard.
quests.question: What will happen to the plant in the cupboard?
options: It will grow faster
It will grow bigger flowers
It will turn into a tree
It will grow weak and pale
quests.correctAnswer: It will grow weak and pale
quests.hint: Plants use light to make their own food.
quests.explanation: Plants make food using sunlight, so without it they grow thin, pale and weak.
quests.funFact: Plants make food using sunlight in a process called photosynthesis.

quests.instruction: A gardener says rain helps vegetables more than water from a hose.
quests.question: Why might rainwater be a good drink for plants?
options: It falls widely and soaks in gently
It contains sugar that plants like
It is warmer than tap water
It does not dry up or evaporate
quests.correctAnswer: It falls widely and soaks in gently
quests.hint: Picture how rain reaches every plant at once.
quests.explanation: Rain falls gently over the whole garden, watering lots of plants at once.
quests.funFact: Rainwater has been collected by gardeners for hundreds of years.

quests.instruction: Seeds sleep in dry soil all through a dry season. When the first heavy rains arrive, green shoots appear within days.
quests.question: What woke the seeds?
options: The light of bright stars
The cold of the frost
Water in the soil
A strong gust of wind
quests.correctAnswer: Water in the soil
quests.hint: Seeds need moisture to start growing.
quests.explanation: Water soaks into seeds and tells them it's time to sprout.
quests.funFact: Some desert flowers bloom within days after rare rain.

quests.instruction: During a very hot, dry spell, farmers worry that their crops will wilt.
quests.question: What helps the most?
options: Cutting all the leaves off
Watering them and giving shade
Adding even more sunshine
Sprinkling snow on top of them
quests.correctAnswer: Watering them and giving shade
quests.hint: Plants need to lose less water and get more to drink.
quests.explanation: Giving water and a little shade helps plants cope with heat.
quests.funFact: Some plants curl their leaves in dry weather to lose less water.

quests.instruction: After days of heavy rain, a field is under water and the young plants look yellow.
quests.question: What is the likely problem?
options: Roots are getting far too little water
The leaves are getting far too much sun
Wind has dried all of the plants out
Roots get too much water, too little air
quests.correctAnswer: Roots get too much water, too little air
quests.hint: Roots need air as well as water.
quests.explanation: Waterlogged soil has no air, so roots cannot breathe and plants suffer.
quests.funFact: Some plants, like rice, are specially adapted to grow in standing water.

quests.instruction: Every autumn, many birds fly to warmer places for the winter.
quests.question: Why do birds migrate?
options: Because the wind makes them
Because leaves block the Sun for them
To reach the Sun
To find food and milder weather
quests.correctAnswer: To find food and milder weather
quests.hint: Imagine what food is available in winter.
quests.explanation: In winter, insects and plants can be scarce, so many birds travel to places with more food.
quests.funFact: The Arctic tern flies from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back every year.

quests.instruction: A bear eats a great deal in autumn and then sleeps for much of winter.
quests.question: What is this sleep called?
options: Condensation
Migration
Hibernation
Evaporation
quests.correctAnswer: Hibernation
quests.hint: Animals save energy when food is hard to find.
quests.explanation: Hibernation helps animals use very little energy when winter weather makes food scarce.
quests.funFact: Some hibernating animals' heartbeats slow down to just a few beats a minute.

quests.instruction: In hot weather, a dog pants with its tongue out.
quests.question: Why does it do this?
options: To smell the air better
To cool down
To catch the breeze
To warm its tongue
quests.correctAnswer: To cool down
quests.hint: Dogs don't sweat like people do.
quests.explanation: Panting lets water evaporate from the tongue and mouth, which carries heat away.
quests.funFact: Dogs have sweat glands in their paws, but panting is their main way to cool.

quests.instruction: Elephants use their ears like fans on very hot days.
quests.question: How does flapping their ears help?
options: It keeps flies away from the face
It makes shade for the calves
It makes noise to signal the herd
Blood in the ears cools in moving air
quests.correctAnswer: Blood in the ears cools in moving air
quests.hint: Moving air cools skin.
quests.explanation: Elephants' large ears have many blood vessels, so flapping them cools the blood.
quests.funFact: African elephants have larger ears than Asian elephants, which helps them lose heat.

quests.instruction: Some animals grow thicker fur in autumn.
quests.question: Why is thick fur useful in winter?
options: It makes the animal heavier
It traps warm air close to the body
It keeps rain away from the body
It makes the animals brighter
quests.correctAnswer: It traps warm air close to the body
quests.hint: Focus on how layers of clothing work.
quests.explanation: Thick fur traps a layer of air that is warmed by the animal's body.
quests.funFact: Arctic foxes have some of the warmest fur of any mammal.

quests.instruction: In very cold places, some fish stay alive under the frozen surface of a lake.
quests.question: Why can they survive?
options: The fish turn to ice and wake in spring
The water below is always warm like a bath
The ice on top protects the water below
The fish dig deep holes in the ice
quests.correctAnswer: The ice on top protects the water below
quests.hint: Remember that ice floats.
quests.explanation: Ice floats and forms a layer on top, which protects the water below so fish can swim.
quests.funFact: Some frogs can survive being partly frozen in winter.

quests.instruction: In spring, the days get warmer, and bees start to visit flowers.
quests.question: Why do many insects become active in spring?
options: Warmth makes them move more
The wind pulls them out
Flowers give off a lot of heat in spring
Spring makes them hungry for snow
quests.correctAnswer: Warmth makes them move more
quests.hint: Insects are affected by temperature.
quests.explanation: Many insects are cold-blooded, so they need warmth to move and feed.
quests.funFact: A bumblebee can shiver its muscles to warm up before flying.

quests.instruction: A snail comes out onto the path after a rainstorm.
quests.question: Why do snails like rainy weather?
options: Damp air stops them drying out
Rain washes their shells clean
Rain makes them grow taller
They feed only on rainwater
quests.correctAnswer: Damp air stops them drying out
quests.hint: Snails need to stay moist.
quests.explanation: Snails need moisture to move and avoid drying, so they appear in damp conditions.
quests.funFact: Snails make a slimy trail that helps them move.

quests.instruction: In the monsoon, frogs begin to croak loudly near ponds.
quests.question: Why do many frogs call more after rain?
options: Rain makes the night warmer for sleeping
Rain makes frogs hungrier
Rain makes ponds where they can breed
Rain makes their skin dry out
quests.correctAnswer: Rain makes ponds where they can breed
quests.hint: Frogs lay eggs in water.
quests.explanation: Rain fills ponds and puddles, giving frogs places to lay eggs, and males call to attract mates.
quests.funFact: Some frogs lay eggs in temporary pools that appear after rain.

quests.instruction: A farmer notices that wind has blown seeds across the field to a new corner.
quests.question: How does wind help some plants?
options: It cools the petals on hot days
It carries their seeds to new places
It waters their leaves each morning
It warms their roots in winter
quests.correctAnswer: It carries their seeds to new places
quests.hint: Remember dandelion seeds.
quests.explanation: Wind scatters seeds so plants can grow in new places.
quests.funFact: Some seeds have wings or fluff that help them fly on the wind.

quests.instruction: A strong storm bends a young tree, but it springs back.
quests.question: Why can young trees often survive strong wind?
options: Their trunks are hollow like pipes
Their roots stay above the ground
They bend instead of breaking
They have no leaves to catch the wind
quests.correctAnswer: They bend instead of breaking
quests.hint: Bending is safer than snapping.
quests.explanation: Young, flexible trunks bend with the wind and spring back.
quests.funFact: Trees grow stronger wood where they are pushed by wind.

quests.instruction: A hot summer makes a pond shrink, and a heron has to walk farther to find fish.
quests.question: How does weather change life at a pond?
options: Fish move into the shallow mud
Less water leaves less room for fish
The pond grows much bigger in the heat
More clouds start to form over the pond
quests.correctAnswer: Less water leaves less room for fish
quests.hint: Notice what shrinking does to habitats.
quests.explanation: As evaporation shrinks ponds, there is less space and food for animals.
quests.funFact: Some fish bury themselves in mud to survive when ponds dry up.

quests.instruction: A cactus in the desert stores water in its thick stem.
quests.question: Why is this useful?
options: It saves water for dry times
It makes the cactus grow tall
It makes shade for other plants
It keeps the cactus warm at night
quests.correctAnswer: It saves water for dry times
quests.hint: Consider places where rain is scarce.
quests.explanation: Cacti store water in their stems and survive for long periods without rain.
quests.funFact: Some cacti can live for hundreds of years.

quests.instruction: Palm trees on a beach have flexible leaves.
quests.question: How do flexible leaves help in storms?
options: They block the wind completely
They are fixed stiff to the trunk
They trap rain to drink
They bend and let wind pass through
quests.correctAnswer: They bend and let wind pass through
quests.hint: Picture a flag in a storm.
quests.explanation: Flexible leaves let strong wind pass through instead of snapping.
quests.funFact: Coconut palms can survive many storms by bending.

quests.instruction: In a rainforest, trees grow very tall and leaves have pointed tips.
quests.question: What does the pointed tip help with?
options: Rainwater drips off quickly
It keeps leaves cold
It makes the leaf heavier
It catches more wind
quests.correctAnswer: Rainwater drips off quickly
quests.hint: Too much water can harm leaves.
quests.explanation: Drip tips help leaves shed water, which keeps them healthy in very rainy places.
quests.funFact: Rainforests may get more than two metres of rain a year.

quests.instruction: In winter, a pond freezes and a duck stays on the open water at the edge.
quests.question: Why do ducks stay near unfrozen water?
options: They need the ice to build their nests
They can still find food there
They can only sleep on moving water
They are chasing after the Sun
quests.correctAnswer: They can still find food there
quests.hint: Imagine food and water.
quests.explanation: Open water gives ducks access to food, so they stay where it is available.
quests.funFact: Ducks' feathers are coated with oil that keeps them dry.

quests.instruction: Squirrels collect and hide acorns in autumn.
quests.question: What are they preparing for?
options: A rainy afternoon later today
A summer storm that is coming
A windy morning in spring
Winter, when food will be scarce
quests.correctAnswer: Winter, when food will be scarce
quests.hint: Focus on the season that comes next.
quests.explanation: Squirrels store food in autumn so they can eat during cold months.
quests.funFact: Squirrels often forget some acorns, which grow into new trees.

quests.instruction: Some animals' coats change colour with the seasons.
quests.question: Why might a hare turn white in winter?
options: To blend in with snow
To look bigger
To attract the Sun
To stay warm
quests.correctAnswer: To blend in with snow
quests.hint: Remember hiding from predators.
quests.explanation: A white coat helps a hare hide in snow from animals that hunt it.
quests.funFact: Arctic hares and ptarmigan change colour with the seasons.

quests.instruction: A farmer is checking clouds and the sky before sowing seeds.
quests.question: Why do farmers care about weather forecasts?
options: Weather decides what colour crops are
Rain, heat and frost affect how crops grow
Farmers make the weather themselves
Forecasts tell the plants when to grow
quests.correctAnswer: Rain, heat and frost affect how crops grow
quests.hint: Notice what plants need.
quests.explanation: Forecasts help farmers choose when to plant, water and harvest.
quests.funFact: Some farmers use rain gauges and weather stations on their fields.

quests.instruction: A gardener covers young tomato plants with cloth on a night when frost is forecast.
quests.question: Why?
options: To make them grow taller overnight
To give them extra sunshine
To feed them with rain
To protect them from the frost
quests.correctAnswer: To protect them from the frost
quests.hint: Cold can damage soft leaves.
quests.explanation: Covers trap a little heat and keep frost off the leaves.
quests.funFact: Young tomato plants can be killed by a single frost.

quests.instruction: After a wet spring, a farmer sees lots of weeds and mud in the field.
quests.question: Why do weeds grow quickly in wet, warm weather?
options: Mud is made out of seeds
Rain makes weeds grow only at night
Clouds feed the weeds
Water and warmth help all plants grow
quests.correctAnswer: Water and warmth help all plants grow
quests.hint: Plants need the same things.
quests.explanation: Weeds respond to water and warmth just as crops do, so they grow fast in wet weather.
quests.funFact: Some weed seeds can stay in soil for decades.

quests.instruction: A park ranger notes that plants grow slowly in a cold, shady, dry spot.
quests.question: Which weather features slow down plants?
options: Cold, dry and little light
Warm, wet and humid
Warm, moist and bright
Mild, wet and sunny
quests.correctAnswer: Cold, dry and little light
quests.hint: Combine temperature, water and light.
quests.explanation: Plants grow best with warmth, water and light, so lacking these slows them.
quests.funFact: Alpine plants grow low and slow in the cold.

quests.instruction: A forest stays green all year, with plenty of rain and warm temperatures.
quests.question: What kind of weather is this?
options: Cold and snowy
Cold and dry
Warm and wet
Hot and dry
quests.correctAnswer: Warm and wet
quests.hint: Consider what makes plants thrive.
quests.explanation: Warm temperatures and lots of rain make forests lush and green all year.
quests.funFact: Tropical rainforests cover a small part of Earth but are home to a huge share of its plant and animal species.

quests.instruction: A student writes that weather affects both plants and animals.
quests.question: Which example shows this?
options: Wind has no colour at all anywhere
Clouds look white against the sky
Birds migrate when food runs short
Rain falls down from the clouds above
quests.correctAnswer: Birds migrate when food runs short
quests.hint: Find an example with a living thing responding.
quests.explanation: Many animals change what they do based on weather and seasons.
quests.funFact: Many animals sense changes in daylight and temperature.
